newsitem.title: USA: CME board elects Melamed as exchange adviser.
newsitem.headline: CME board elects Melamed as exchange adviser.

text.p: Chicago Mercantile Exchange board members elected Leo Melamed, CME chairman emeritus, to the newly created post of permanent adviser to the board late Wednesday, the exchange said.
The new position again gives Melamed, who retired from exchange governance in 1991 after nearly 25 years, a voice in the direction of the exchange.
That direction could be changing, according to some members. Six of the 12 seats on the 34-member board filled in an exchange election last week were first-time directors.
Five incumbents were voted out of office and one retired.

"This last election was a clear mandate for change," Melamed said in an interview. He said the outcome was "kind of a revolutionary demand by the membership for change and a change in direction and dissatisfaction with the status quo."
He said sentiment in favor of his return was "enormous."

"The fact that there is this demand, that there are so many new faces, was bound to make a difference," he said about his decision to accept the new position. Melamed is currently chairman and chief executive officer of Sakura Dellsher Inc, a global futures firm.
"And I think when I'm added to the mix, it clearly will change -- we hope -- some of the direction of the exchange," Melamed said. "There is no magic wand, though."
Melamed's unpaid position as adviser to the board and executive committee does not carry any voting privileges.
Members have expressed concerns in recent years about declines in both CME trading volume and seat prices, and about a lack of technological development at the exchange.
Some members said those concerns may have contributed to the election of six new board members.
Two of the new directors, William Shepard and Joel Stender, were active in the Equity Owners Association, which has published newsletters in the last year criticizing the leadership at the exchange.
Melamed, who was not present at Wednesday's board meeting, said Scott Gordon, first vice chairman, issued the motion which was approved almost unanimously.
"I welcome him (Melamed) back and look forward to his return in an advisory capacity to the board," CME chairman Jack Sandner said through an exchange spokesman.
Sandner was re-elected in last week's election and has one more year to complete his two-year term as CME chairman.

In a letter to members dated Thursday, Sandner said that in the first quarter of 1997 the board will discuss issues ranging from the size of the Standard & Poor's 500 contract to restructuring committees to Internet order routing. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
